Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting additional promo credits & brief extension of trial

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the great demo last week — the team is excited about the latency gains. We hit a blocker during integration and burned through our initial trial credits while trying multiple connection configs.

Could Redwood grant an extra $1,000 worth of promo credits and extend our trial by two weeks so we can finish the integration and validate latency at scale?

We're a small engineering team (2 EEs + 1 MLE) and the delays were internal: a misconfigured VPC endpoint and a dependency mismatch that stalled our perf tests. I attached the credit_request_form with our details.

Attached: credit_request_form.pdf

Happy to provide logs or a short recording of the failed runs if helpful. We want to move to a paid pilot after we verify throughput in our staging environment.

Best,
Samir Patel
CTO, EdgeAI

Hi Samir — great to hear the demo resonated.

Thanks for the context and for sending the form. Two quick asks to help me escalate this for an exception:

- Can you send a short summary of what consumed the credits (approx token counts / endpoints hit / date ranges)?
- Are there other EdgeAI accounts or email aliases that may have been used for earlier trials?

I want to be transparent: we do review repeated trial/top-up patterns before approving extra credits. I'm looping in Marissa from Billing and Neha from Trust to do a quick check. If there are no concerning signals, we can approve a one-time $1k promo credit and a two-week extension as a pilot credit. If there are suspicious patterns, we may need to triage via fraud review.

Next steps:
- Samir: send the usage snapshot and any related account emails.
- Marissa: can you pull billing/trial history for EdgeAI?
- Neha: will run a pattern check and advise.

Thanks — I'll follow up once we have the checks.

Cheers,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Team, Samir — I completed a quick fraud review and pattern analysis. Summary below and recommendation: 

Summary of findings:
- Confirmed three distinct Redwood accounts under @edgeai.io in the last 90 days (IDs redacted in this thread). Two of the accounts show multiple trial credit requests within 10–20 day windows.
- One of the secondary accounts used a different billing name but the same testing IP range (172.56.8.*) on key days, suggesting the same org's test infra.
- The primary account shows the token spike Marissa referenced; logs indicate batch job runs rather than interactive usage.

Conclusion & decision:
Given the repeated trial-topup pattern across multiple accounts and shared IP ranges, this looks like coordinated re-requests to extend free usage rather than a single integration mishap. I am declining the one-time promo exception for an unrestricted credit extension.

Offer to mitigate:
- Approve a monitored, conservative paid pilot: provision $300 of pilot credits (chargeable) and a 7-day monitored window with usage alerts and a dedicated SE check-in. This balances risk while keeping the deal live.
- If EdgeAI can provide a short integration runbook and confirm sole ownership of the accounts, we will reevaluate a second, time-limited promo credit.

Attached: fraud_review_summary.pdf

Samir — if you'd like to accept the paid pilot option I can ask Marissa to issue an invoice and Sean to schedule the SE check. If you disagree, please reply with additional evidence of separate teams or partners that might explain the multiple signups.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Trust Analyst
Redwood Inference
